1.he: ואך מ / הדפ / לזכות את הר / עד ש
1.note: The left edge of this page is cut off in the scanned copy, so the end of each line is lost: "only a f…" (ואך מ, probably "only a few"), "therefore … print…" (הדפ), "to bring merit to the …" (את הר, probably "the public"), and the number of years of the reprint ban (עד ש…). The gaps are marked […]; the missing words are not supplied.

2.note: "A young man" is the usual humble self-description. אי"ש is printed with abbreviation marks, so it may also hide the initials of the editor, who signs at the end as ישע"ה (Isaiah); not resolved.

3.note: The Livorno editor opens with "the book of the paths of life" (orḥot ḥayyim), a play on the Ḥida's first name Ḥayyim; the book is named Ma'agal Tov a few lines below. The right edge of this page is torn in the scanned copy, so many lines lose their first word or letters; gaps are marked […].

4.he: ביד זרע רב ה"ה הח"הש ר' / ה כ"ע
4.note: The grandson's name falls at the torn start of a line: only ...ה and the abbreviation כ"ע remain. ה"ה is read as "namely" (הלא הוא) and הח"הש as "the sage" (perhaps החכם השלם, "the perfect sage"); כ"ע is not resolved. He is the son of R. Isaiah Azulai, the Ḥida's son.

5.note: "Going about" ends one line and ימותו ("his days"?) begins the next after the torn edge; the words between are lost, and the reading ימותו is not certain.

6.he: את כל הקורות דבר בע"טו קש"תו ככס"רת
6.note: Rhymed prose with abbreviation marks inside the words, perhaps marking a wordplay or a chronogram. דבר בעטו is read as דבר בעתו, "a word in its season" (Prov 15:23, which goes on "how good it is", tov, the title word). קש"תו and ככס"רת (on the scan perhaps כנס"רת) are not understood and are left untranslated.

7.note: The Hebrew paragraph begins in the middle of the editor's sentence. "In order" reads והסדר"ת as a form of סדר (perhaps כסדרת, "in sequence"); the abbreviation marks are not explained.

8.note: תמתו begins a line after the torn edge; letters before it are probably lost. Not translated.

9.he: על כל / ות סודו לה' כי טוב
9.note: The start of the line is lost (…ות, perhaps "the good things"). סודו is read as הודו ("give thanks"), the opening of Ps 136:1; ה and ס look much alike in this type.

10.he: ובהיותו רב / נאי קדוש יאמר לו
10.note: "When he was rabbi" ends a line; the next line begins …נאי after the torn edge, so the words between are lost (perhaps the name of a place or community). The later …ת אנקונא has also lost its start (perhaps "the holy congregation of Ancona").

11.note: "His grandson" is the Ḥida's grandson named above. הר"ת is not resolved (perhaps "the rabbi R. T…"). An Abraham Ḥai Musafia of Ancona was the Ḥida's friend in 1776 (part 2); the man who came to Livorno in 1867 must be a later bearer of the name, perhaps a descendant. As printed, it is Musafia who saw the manuscript in Ancona and the editor who met him in Livorno.

12.note: The phrase is Lam 2:8 "he did not draw back his hand from swallowing" (לא השיב ידו מבלע); only the last letter of the verb survives the torn edge.

13.note: Wordplay: Ruth 2:7 has "to glean among the sheaves" (ba-omarim); the editor spells it באומרים, "among the sayings", with abbreviation marks to point to the pun. The next phrase "…טי בתר ליקוטי" (gleanings after gleanings, Aramaic) has lost its first letters; "as bees do" (הדבו"רים, Deut 1:44) plays on devorim "bees" and dibburim "words".

14.note: Printed תהר"א; read as מהר"א, "our teacher R. A[braham]" (Musafia), with מ misprinted or misread as ת; suspected error. After it, the end of the line (ל…) is lost.

15.note: Printed להיפים ("to beautify"?); read as להדפיס, "to print", which the context requires (the type makes ה/ס and ם/ס look alike). Suspected misprint or misreading.

16.note: The title's first letters are lost at the torn edge; probably Tehillah le-David ("A praise of David", Ps 145:1), a work on Psalms. ע"ם is read as "on the Book of Psalms" (על ספר?). Not checked in bibliographies.

17.note: צריק is read as צדיק, "a righteous man" (ד and ר are close in this type).

18.note: The start of the line is lost (…יתי, perhaps "I saw"). כנהו is not clear (perhaps "his stock", cf. Ps 80:16, or כחו "his strength"); left untranslated.

19.note: The start of the line is lost (…ות, perhaps "to show"). בכ"י is read as בני כלל ישראל, "all Israel"; not certain. The line before also lost its first word after חשקה ("[my …] longed").

20.he: כ"ד הצעיר מקי"ר ע"ה ישע"ה ס"ט
20.note: כ"ד = "these are the words of". מקי"ר and ע"ה are not resolved (ע"ה perhaps "servant of the Lord" or "dust and ashes", a humble formula). ישע"ה is the name Isaiah, printed as an abbreviation. ס"ט = ספרדי טהור, "pure Sephardi", a usual signature of Sephardi rabbis, also used by the Ḥida below.

21.he: ושיכויי דחיקי. ובוקי סריקי. שאין האים מכוקם
21.note: Aramaic rhymed prose. שיכויי is read as "thorns" (cf. Num 33:55 שכים); בוקי סריקי ("empty flasks") is a Talmudic phrase for worthless people. שאין האים מכוקם is not understood (perhaps a misprint), and the end of the line is cut off; left untranslated.

22.note: Abbreviation not resolved; perhaps a phrase about being saved from distress. Left untranslated.

23.note: The left edge of this page is cut off in the scanned copy, so the last word of several lines is lost or broken: אות… ("sign"), היתה ל…, על…, הנ(ס)…, ופי…, כהי…, ברכ…. The gaps are marked […].

24.note: העבור is read as "what passed" over me (העבור עלי), with abbreviation marks perhaps pointing to a pun (also "intercalation" or "pregnancy"). The word after על is lost at the cut edge.

25.he: ואת הנ"ס למינהו על חד מאה בדשערוהי
25.note: "After its kind" (למינהו) is Genesis wording. בדשערוהי is read as Aramaic "than what he estimated" (שער "to estimate"); not certain.

26.he: לאל העושה כהור עכני סגיאן מלוהי
26.note: כהור עכני is not understood (perhaps a misprint for an Aramaic phrase such as "with me", עמי); left untranslated. סגיאן מלוהי is Aramaic "many are His words (or deeds)".

27.note: The end of the line (כהי…) is cut, and כאלי is not understood; only "kindnesses upon kindnesses" is clear.

28.he: ועשיתי לו פדיונות וממוני כוסף על אשר עשו מממונו
28.note: Pidyonot, gifts of charity given as "redemption" for a sick man. כוסף is read as כסף (money), meaning that he gave from his own money in addition to what was given from the sick man's; the sentence is hard and the reading is not certain.

29.note: The Muscovite: the Russian fleet in the Mediterranean during the Russo-Turkish war of 1768–1774. ויקף ראש is read as "raised his head" (ויזקוף ראש), that is, grew bold; not certain.

31.note: טבאקו = tobacco (Italian tabacco); שארופי = syrup (Italian sciroppo, Arabic sharāb).

32.he: יו"א תבא בא רשות ויצאנו לשלום
32.note: Permission from the port to land, probably after a quarantine at Sousse (pratique); read so from the context.

33.he: כי לא נח"ם אלהים דרך ארץ
33.note: Wordplay on Exod 13:17 ("God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines"): derekh eretz, "the way of the land", also means good manners. The abbreviation marks on נחם point to the pun.

34.note: Katan is taken as a family name; it could also be read "the young R. Abraham, the warden".

35.note: Family name as printed; the vowels (Ma'arek, Me'arek) are not certain.

36.note: The paragraph ends in the middle of a sentence: the following leaves are lost in this scanned copy. The text resumes in part 1, in Tunis.
